mission: Ben and Desh finally speak about GAG and Jacen, and the Brotherhood ritual resolves in the same quiet space as that confession.
why_now: Torin's warmth-on-a-beat in the previous scene has put the pattern into the air. The conversation Desh has been carrying since Chapter 1 finally has a door to go through. The Brotherhood ritual piece Desh has been reconstructing resolves tonight — and lands in the same silence that holds Jacen's name.
conflict: Both men have carried the same shame for years. Desh forces the conversation not because he wants to talk about Jacen but because Torin has begun to sound like the good version of him, and Desh recognises the voice. Ben is not ready to hear that sentence. Desh says it anyway. At the same time, the Brotherhood ritual framework completes itself on Desh's datapad: the Jedi Lords were not corrupt, they were competent people under catastrophic pressure who made the wrong emergency choice. Two reckonings hold each other up.
turning_point: Desh names the Torin/Jacen sound-likeness in a single short line. Ben's stomach drops because Desh has just said what Ben has been refusing to think. A beat later, the Brotherhood ritual framework resolves on Desh's datapad — right about the emergency, wrong about the cost. Ben registers both together.
opening_hook: Desh doesn't start with Jacen. He starts with a specific day — a raid they both remember, an arrest that went wrong, a face Ben sees when he can't sleep
closing_hook: Neither of them says 'we should watch Torin.' They don't need to. On Desh's datapad, the ritual reconstruction sits in the quiet — the Jedi Lords turned into tragic peers in the same breath Jacen became a named shape in the room
emotional_trajectory: Careful approach -> painful honesty -> Brotherhood framework completing itself -> shared understanding without resolution

stakes.personal: Ben confronting the worst chapter of his life with the only person who shared it, while the Jedi Lords' moral architecture reorganises into tragic-peer shape in the same silence
stakes.interpersonal: Ben/Desh relationship deepening from friendship to trust forged in acknowledged shame
stakes.external: The Jacen pattern recognition will become tactical intelligence; the Brotherhood ritual understanding reframes Gavran from villain to tragic predecessor — both feeds the Ch 13 midpoint and the Ch 21 refusal

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit, night cycle, dim lighting
sensory_details: Dim instrument lights; the quiet of a ship where everyone else is sleeping; Desh's hands on the controls, steady the way they always are; the weight of shared memory pressing the cockpit smaller; Desh's datapad glow at a low setting, the ritual reconstruction resolving in the margin of the larger silence
canon_elements_needed: Brotherhood of Darkness ideology and military doctrine at the Reformations era
vergence-corruption ritual as a named Brotherhood strategic goal
Jedi Lords era emergency containment theory and Gavran's removal-technique rationale
action_beats: Desh keeps his hands steady on the flight controls while describing the raid they both remember
Ben's fingers tighten on the armrest when Desh names the pattern — Torin sounding like the good version of Jacen
The Brotherhood ritual reconstruction resolves on Desh's datapad in the quiet after the Jacen beat — the Weave-polarity flip attempt, Gavran's removal-technique as the cut-off, the cost
Both men stare at instrument readouts they aren't reading through a long silence that holds both reckonings at once
promises_paid: Ben and Desh share unspoken GAG history (PP02)
notes: Let the scene feel like two men setting down weight they have carried too long. The historical revelation should ride beside that emotion, not interrupt it.
